title: Tagging good practice: why `latest` is not a version

videos.script: Latest sounds like the newest version. It is not. It is the tag Docker writes when you leave one out. {{latest}} Ana starts two containers from the same name, a few seconds apart, and they run two different versions. Nothing in either command says so. {{scheme}} So this lesson builds a scheme. One build gets four tags: the release, the minor line, the major line, and the commit. A patch release moves two of them, and leaves the other two where they were. {{overwrite}} Then Ana pushes over a release tag, and the registry lets her. {{digest}} Which is why the bases in the Dockerfile, and the image a deployment starts, are named by digest.
